title: Claude only on this machine: OpenAI blocked by a setting, its key kept; a run that never read .env reaches Claude too
request: The owner: 'use only claude model not openai model but do not delete it'.
spec: Every real model client is created behind models/live_guard.check; every tier is resolved by models/settings.tier.
plan: Block by a setting at the one place every client is created, and at tier resolution.
Make a live process that never read .env take the owner's settings from it.
Keep tests unchanged: they never read .env.

decisions.decision: DCLAB_BLOCK_PROVIDERS=openai in .env, not deleting the OpenAI key or settings.
decisions.why: The owner asked to keep them; a block is reversible by one line.

decisions.decision: A provider is known by its hosts (openai.com); a local server is never blocked.
decisions.why: Ollama and LM Studio speak OpenAI's protocol on localhost; blocking the protocol would block them.

decisions.decision: owner_value: the process's own value first (an empty one counts), else .env, never inside a test.
decisions.why: The test runner blanks the owner's settings; a command-line run that never read .env had taken the OpenAI key from the shell.

decisions.decision: The research campaign's own OpenAI endpoints are guarded too.
decisions.why: agents.py, live_eval.py and guide_review.py build clients outside the gateway.

change: dclab_rnd/models/live_guard.py (BLOCK, owner_value, blocked, ProviderBlocked, the check), models/settings.py (owner settings, a blocked tier unavailable), agentic/agents.py, live_eval.py, guide_review.py, .env.example, tests/run_parallel.py, tests/test_provider_block.py; .env (the owner's, not committed).

findings.defect: A command-line run asked OpenAI with the owner's key while the product's model is Claude.
findings.scenario: The collector's first trial: 155 decision questions to gpt-5.6-terra (60,039 input and 5,798 output tokens), unpriced, recorded as Claude's.
findings.cause: The tier settings read only the process environment; the command line had not read .env, so DCLAB_LLM_PROVIDER was unset and the shell's OPENAI_API_KEY served.
findings.fix: owner_value reads .env for a live process; DCLAB_BLOCK_PROVIDERS=openai refuses every OpenAI client and makes its tiers unavailable.

measurements.name: a run from the owner's shell with the OpenAI key present and .env unread
measurements.gate: affected tests only (the owner's daytime rule)
measurements.result: every tier claude-sonnet-5-5; a tier pointed at OpenAI unavailable with no key sent; a direct OpenAI client refused; a local Ollama client allowed; 262 tests in 17 files pass
limits: a tool that reads OPENAI_API_KEY without DCLab's clients is not covered

outcome: No request leaves this machine for OpenAI; the OpenAI key and settings stay in .env.
lessons: A setting a server reads from .env must be read the same way by every command-line run, or the two reach different models.
risks: Removing the block line re-enables OpenAI at once.
